title: OperationalDNA
description:
A complete Operational DNA document for a business. Operational DNA describes organizational modeling — what the org is and what it does, independent of UI, API, or deployment technology. Modeled around the Actor > Action > Subject triad: Positions act, Subjects (Resource | Person | Position | Group) receive actions.

Organized in three categories:
- People: Person, Position, Group, Membership
- Structures: Resource, Attribute, Relationship
- Activities: Operation, Task, Step, Process, Trigger, Rule

Every primitive lives in a top-level collection (resources/persons/positions/groups and the activities). A primitive names its home Domain via its `domain` reference. `domain` is the thin tenant-root node; descendant domains live in the flat `domains[]`, each naming its `parent`.

domain.description: The organization / tenant root Domain — a thin node (no contained primitives). Exactly one root; descendant domains live in the top-level `domains[]` and name their `parent`.

domains.description: The descendant (non-root) Domains, as a flat list of thin nodes. Each names its `parent`; the hierarchy is the parent-edge chain, not inline nesting.

resources.description: Resource type definitions. Each names its home Domain via `domain`.

persons.description: Person type definitions. Each names its home Domain via `domain`.

positions.description: Position type definitions. Each names its home Domain via `domain`.

groups.description: Group type definitions. Each names its home Domain via `domain`.

memberships.description: Template-level eligibility statements: which Person types may hold which Positions in which Groups.

operations.description: All Subject.Action operation pairs defined in this domain — the atomic units of business activity. Subject is any noun primitive (Resource, Person, Position, Group).

triggers.description: What initiates each Operation or Process — user actions, schedules, webhooks, chained operations.

rules.description: Constraints on operations — who may perform them (access rules) and what conditions must be satisfied (condition rules). Condition rules are also referenced by Step.conditions[] for compositional gating.

relationships.description: Named, directed connections between noun primitives — formalizes the semantic link a reference Attribute implies, adding cardinality.

tasks.description: Atomic reusable units of business activity: a Position performing exactly one Operation.

processes.description: Standard Operating Procedures — named, owned DAGs of Steps that accomplish business goals. Each Process declares an explicit `startStep` (Amazon-States-Language convention).
